samples.summary: `canUndo`/`canRedo` read-only guard is asserted vacuously (fresh store has no history anyway)
samples.evidence: `initialize` now returns `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:672-674). The new test `lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount` asserts `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` / `canRedo()).toBe(false)` on a `new MemNoteStore('hello')` whose undo and redo stacks are empty, so `store.canUndo()` is already `false` and the assertion holds identically with the `!readOnly &&` prefix removed. To exercise the guard the store would have to carry history (e.g. `store.editText(...)`/`store.undo()` on the raw store before `initialize`). Consequence if the guard regresses: a read-only mount reports an undoable state and the host toolbar offers an enabled undo/redo control that does nothing.

samples.summary: 'neuters every write path' does not observe the neutering of `setLocalSelection` / `recordSelectionForHistory`
samples.evidence: In `it('neuters every write path')` the calls `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` and `view.recordSelectionForHistory({anchor:0,head:0})` are followed only by `expect(store.getText()).toBe('hello')` and `expect(store.canUndo()).toBe(false)`. Neither assertion changes if those two mutators were forwarded to the target — `MemNoteStore` records them into the private `currentSelection`/`batchAfterSelection`, which the test never reads (e.g. via an undo unit's restored selection) and no spy covers. So the wrapper's deliberate suppression of the presence/caret publish (documented at packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:138-143) has no failing case; a regression that republished a viewer's caret to peers would pass. A spy-backed fake `NoteStore` (assert `not.toHaveBeenCalled()`) would close it.
searchedFor: read memory.ts to look for an observable effect

samples.summary: The divider drag/hit-area change (25px width, `touch-action: none`, new `track` ratio math) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: The diff changes the split divider from 7px to a 25px hit area, adds `touchAction = 'none'`, and changes the drag math from `(ev.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width` to `/ (rect.width - divider.offsetWidth)` — a user-visible pointer-tracking change. I grepped `divider|splitRatio|pointerdown|pointermove|note-divider|col-resize` across packages/notes/src (only editor.ts matches) and across packages/frontend/tests (no matches), and `note-divider` appears in exactly one file repo-wide. `packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts` covers view-mode switching but never dispatches a pointer sequence on the divider, so neither the new ratio formula nor the touch-drag enablement is exercised; a sign/denominator error would ship silently (the panes would jump or the divider would trail the pointer).

samples.summary: The frontend mount's own `readOnlyNoteStore` wrap (and the `storeRef` type widening) has no test
samples.evidence: `notes-view.tsx` now does `const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw` and stores it in a `NoteStore`-typed ref used by the thumbnail's `getText()`. There is no `notes-view.test.tsx` — packages/frontend/src/app/notes contains only notes-toolbar.test.tsx, notes-thumbnail.test.ts, yorkie-note-store.test.ts and notes-undo-integration.test.ts, and packages/frontend/tests has no notes-view file. Since packages/frontend runs no `tsc` at all, a mistake here (wrapping a writable mount, or the thumbnail reading a neutered member) is caught by nothing. Engine-level coverage exists for `readOnlyNoteStore` itself, which contains the impact.

samples.evidence: `uploadImage = useMemo(() => (token && !readOnly ? shareTokenImageUploader(token) : undefined))` — shared-notes-layout.test.tsx always renders with `token = "tok-1"` (`renderLayout(role, token = "tok-1")`), so the `!token` arm (a share mount with no token) is never rendered. samples.summary: `NotesView` is mocked wholesale, so the prop contract between layout and view is asserted only against the test's own copy of the names
samples.evidence: `vi.mock("@/app/notes/notes-view")` replaces the component with a recorder, and the wiring tests assert `viewProps.current.viewMode / readOnly / uploadImage`. That catches a rename inside the layout, but not a divergence from `NotesViewProps` — and packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane, so nothing else would. I checked the real signature (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:30-58) and the names currently match, so this is a durability concern rather than a live gap; `uploadImage` is additionally mocked at `@/app/docs/image-insert`, so 'hands the share-token uploader to the view' proves only that the layout calls the factory with the token.

samples.summary: Shadow-log `target=` formatting covered only for a single well-formed attribute
samples.evidence: The new target string maps every attribute with `${attr?.key ?? '?'}:${attr?.verb ?? '?'}` joined by ','. The only test ('names the document and verb it would have denied') passes exactly one attribute `{key:'note-1',verb:'rw'}` and asserts `target=note-1:rw`; the multi-attribute join and the `'?'` fallbacks for a malformed body have no case.
